text:
The Stars have won three of their last five, and they did not win the chance battle in any of them. That stat is the whole story of Dallas right now: a team getting 42% of the expected goals, the quality of chances, over its last five games, kept afloat by Jake Oettinger. He is 13.8 goals saved above expected this season with five shutouts, and on most nights that has been the difference between a slump and a winning week.

Off the ice, the noise is about Jason Robertson. He is playing another contract year, and TSN's headline this week said he offered "no comment on $125M offer from Kraken," adding that he is happy with the Stars "right now." Whatever happens there, he is still our likeliest Star to score tonight at 38%, level with Wyatt Johnston, who carries a seven-game point streak. Jamie Benn reached 1,000 career points earlier this month, which is the warmer storyline in Dallas.

Utah is the opposite case: a team that has played better than it looks. The Mammoth sit on an even goal difference despite chances worth 17.1 goals more than they have allowed, and they own 57% of the five-on-five expected goals. Finishing and goaltending have cost them, and Sebastian Cossa, projected to start, is at minus 4.7 goals saved above expected. They won 6-5 in a shootout in Nashville last night after coming back from two goals down, so both teams are on the second half of a back-to-back.

Without Nick Schmaltz, Logan Cooley has moved beside Clayton Keller and Dylan Guenther, and he has points in six straight. Keller is one assist from 400 for his career. Utah also takes 4.7 penalties a game, and a Dallas power play with this much skill does not need many invitations.
headline: Oettinger keeps covering for the Stars
